title: One Indian Dead, Three in ICU After Riyadh Airport Attack; Embassy Issues Stay-Indoors Advisory
excerpt: Mohammad Yousuf Ali, a 46-year-old Umrah pilgrim from Hyderabad, died of his injuries while three injured Indians remain in intensive care but stable; the Indian Embassy in Riyadh has told nationals to stay alert and indoors as necessary.
body:
• Mohammad Yousuf Ali, a 46-year-old Umrah pilgrim from Hyderabad's Mehdipatnam, died of injuries sustained in the attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, the Indian Embassy confirmed on Sunday.
  • Three injured Indians are in the ICU but stable, two are in normal hospital wards and the rest have been discharged. In all, 11 Indians were among more than 300 people injured in the attack that killed 12, which Saudi Arabia has blamed on Houthi militants.
  • The embassy has issued an advisory asking all Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain alert, stay indoors as necessary and follow instructions from local authorities — and has promised full support, including repatriation of the deceased's remains, to affected families.

An Indian national injured in the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has died, while three other injured Indians are in intensive care but stable, the Embassy of India in Saudi Arabia said on Sunday, even as the mission issued a stay-indoors advisory for Indian nationals across the kingdom.

Embassy officials have visited every hospital where Indians injured in the attack were admitted, according to an update posted on X by the Indian mission. "As mentioned earlier, 1 Indian national unfortunately passed away today, 3 are in ICU, but stable, 2 more are admitted in normal wards while others have been discharged," the embassy said, thanking Saudi authorities for the medical care provided and assuring the affected families of all possible support.

A Hyderabad family's Umrah journey turns to tragedy

The deceased has been identified as Mohammad Yousuf Ali, a 46-year-old resident of Mehdipatnam in Hyderabad. Ali was at the airport with a 13-member Umrah group, preparing to travel to Medina, when the attack struck, according to IANS. Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi confirmed Ali's death on Sunday night, saying Ali had succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Riyadh.

https://x.com/theinformant_x/status/2108927540999987597

The family's losses run deep. One of Ali's sons, Amaan, is undergoing knee surgery; another son, Wasey, is in hospital after losing three toes; and the family's aunt suffered head injuries and is now out of danger. Ali's wife, Sameera, and daughter, Maryam, were reported safe. "It's been confirmed that Yusuf sahab has passed away in the attack," Owaisi said in his post, adding that he is in touch with Ali's brother-in-law in Riyadh and that the embassy's Deputy Chief of Mission has assured the family of care.

"Deeply grieved at the loss of life of an Indian national in the Riyadh attack. My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. The Embassy will extend all possible assistance."

— S. Jaishankar, External Affairs Minister

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar expressed his condolences in a post on X, while the embassy said it is in touch with the family and "will provide all support for ensuring the early repatriation of mortal remains." Owaisi has urged Jaishankar to extend every possible assistance to the bereaved family.

An attack with a heavy toll

The strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, damaging terminal structures and forcing the suspension of some flights. At least 11 Indians are among the injured, according to the Indian embassy. Saudi Arabia has blamed Houthi militants for the attack, and earlier coverage by The Videshi reported that global condemnation has grown, with the United States weighing joining Saudi strikes.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=emC8gRkMJOE

The incident comes amid an escalating confrontation in the region, including recent attacks on commercial shipping in the Gulf that have also put Indian seafarers in harm's way. For the Indian diaspora, Riyadh is one of the largest single hubs of Indian workers abroad, making the airport attack and the embassy's response an immediate community concern.

Embassy advisory: stay alert, stay indoors

Alongside the casualty update, the Embassy of India in Riyadh issued a formal advisory urging Indian nationals in the kingdom to stay alert and vigilant in view of the prevailing situation. The advisory asks Indians to "stay indoors as necessary and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels."

For families back in India with relatives working or travelling in Saudi Arabia, the advisory is the operative instruction: movements should be limited to essential travel, official Saudi government channels should be the only source of guidance on restrictions or curfews, and anyone who needs help should contact the Indian Embassy in Riyadh directly rather than relying on social media forwards. Indians with family members in Saudi Arabia who are travelling for Umrah should confirm flight schedules with their airlines before heading to the airport, as the attack forced diversions and cancellations.

What comes next

The embassy is coordinating with Saudi hospital authorities and the family on repatriation of Yousuf Ali's remains to India. Medical updates on the three Indians in the ICU will determine the next phase of the mission's response. Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia should monitor the embassy's official X handle, @IndianEmbRiyadh, for the next advisory updates. The attack itself has already drawn international condemnation, and India's diplomatic posture will be watched closely as Saudi Arabia weighs its response — read our earlier coverage of world condemnation of the Riyadh airport attack for the full picture.
